name: OPA310IDCKR
title: OPA310, OPA2310, OPA4310 (and S shutdown versions): 1.5 V to 5.5 V rail-to-rail I/O, 3 MHz, high-output-current op amps
summary: Single, dual and quad CMOS op amps for 1.5 V to 5.5 V supplies, with inputs and outputs that reach both rails, 3 MHz gain bandwidth and 165 µA typical per channel. The output stage delivers ±150 mA typical short-circuit current at 5.5 V and has current limiting and thermal shutdown. The inputs have no ESD diode to V+, include EMI filtering and show no phase reversal. The S versions add an active-low shutdown that turns the amplifier on in about 1 µs and leaves the output high impedance when off.
key_figures: 0.100 µA to 0.265 µA per amplifier typ

circuits.title: LED / EML biasing with current sense
circuits.description: Channel 1 of an OPA2310 is a unity-gain follower: a DAC sets its noninverting input and its output drives the LED (or electro-absorption modulated laser) through a series sense resistor RS. Channel 2 is a difference amplifier across RS: R3 from the driven end of RS to IN2+ with R4 to ground, R1 from the LED end of RS to IN2- with R2 from OUT2 back to IN2-. Its output, proportional to the LED current, goes to an MCU. No values are given.

circuits.title: Driving a capacitive load through an isolation resistor
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower with a resistor Riso between the output pin and the load capacitor Cload; VOUT is taken at the capacitor. Feedback is taken from the amplifier output pin, before Riso. A series resistor of typically 10 Ω to 20 Ω cuts the overshoot and ringing a large capacitive load causes; with a resistive load across Cload, Riso and that load form a divider that costs gain and swing.

circuits.title: Low-side current sensing
circuits.description: The load current flows from VBUS through the load and a 0.1 Ω shunt to ground. The amplifier, on a single 5 V supply, is a noninverting stage on the shunt voltage with RF = 57.6 kΩ and RG = 1.2 kΩ, a gain of 49 V/V, so 0 A to 1 A gives 0 V to about 4.9 V at VOUT with at most 100 mV across the shunt.

circuits.title: Noninverting amplifier for the SC70 (DCK) layout example
circuits.description: A noninverting stage in the 5-pin SC70: INPUT to IN+ (pin 1); R1 with C1 across it from OUT (pin 4) to IN- (pin 3), and R2 from IN- to ground; R3 and C2 make an RC low-pass from OUT to OUTPUT. C3 bypasses V- (pin 2) and C4 bypasses V+ (pin 5) to ground. No values are given.

operation.text: OPA310 is single, OPA2310 dual and OPA4310 quad. The S versions (OPA310S, OPA2310S, OPA4310S) add shutdown pins. All run from 1.5 V to 5.5 V with inputs and outputs that reach both rails, 3 MHz gain bandwidth and about 165 µA per channel.
Full specification covers 1.8 V to 5.5 V; operation from 1.5 V to 1.8 V is tested. Many limits hold from –40°C to 125°C. Above 7 V across the supply the part can be destroyed.

Each supply pin takes a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor to ground, placed right at the device; in a single-supply design the one on V+ is enough. The supply pins are to be bypassed with no less than 0.01 µF ceramic.

The input has a P-channel pair and an N-channel pair in parallel. The P pair works from (V–) to about (V+) – 0.4 V, the N pair from there to the positive rail; both conduct over a transition band typically (V+) – 0.5 V to (V+) – 0.3 V. With process spread that band can sit anywhere from (V+) – 0.7 V…(V+) – 0.5 V to (V+) – 0.3 V…(V+) – 0.1 V. Offset, drift, PSRR, CMRR and THD are worse inside the band. Performance is slightly better on the P pair, whose range reaches to 0.7 V from V+ (1.4 V on the TLV900x).

A class AB stage with common-source output transistors swings rail to rail. At 5.5 V and room temperature with loads of 2 kΩ or lighter it comes within 20 mV of either rail. Short-circuit current is at least ±75 mA across temperature at 5.5 V; outputs may be paralleled for more current. Current limiting and thermal shutdown protect the output.

As a unity-gain buffer the amplifier holds about 40° phase margin with 75 pF of pure capacitance and does not oscillate continuously up to 250 pF. More closed-loop gain tolerates more capacitance. Capacitors over about 1 µF can have enough ESR to keep the loop stable. A 10 Ω to 20 Ω series output resistor reduces overshoot and ringing with large loads.
When the output saturates, it takes about 0.75 µs typical to return to linear operation, after which it slews at the normal rate; the total delay is the recovery time plus the slew time.
The inputs have built-in RF filtering. EMIRR referred to IN+ is characterized from 10 MHz to 6 GHz.

The input ESD cells have no steering diode to V+, so a signal may be present at an input before V+ comes up without a path into the positive supply. The inputs are clamped to V–. Steering diodes on the inputs, output and SHDN lead to an internal absorption device between the supply rails and stay off in normal use.

The SHDN pins on the S versions are active low and referenced to V–. Logic low is V– to (V–) + 0.2 V; logic high is (V–) + 1.2 V to V+. The threshold is about 500 mV above V– regardless of supply, with hysteresis. Do not drive SHDN above (V+) + 0.5 V, and do not leave it floating. In shutdown the amplifier draws under 500 nA typical at room temperature and its output is high impedance, so outputs can share a bus. Duals have one SHDN per channel; quads have one per pair of channels. Enable and disable take under about 1 µs; disable time lengthens with higher load resistance, and the specified time assumes 10 kΩ to VS / 2. SHDN inputs are high-impedance CMOS.

On packages with an exposed pad (WSON DSG, WQFN RTE) the die is attached to the pad with conductive material, so the pad must be tied to V– and to nothing else; tied elsewhere, the part may not meet its specifications.
The non-S parts are on whenever the supply is between 1.5 V (±0.75 V) and 5.5 V (±2.75 V). The S parts add the shutdown mode.

Keep input traces short and away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles where they must cross. Place the gain resistors close to the inverting input to keep its parasitic capacitance low. Use a ground plane and keep analog and digital ground currents apart. A low-impedance driven guard ring around high-impedance nodes cuts leakage. Clean the board after assembly; after aqueous cleaning bake it, for example 30 minutes at 85°C, to drive out absorbed moisture.
The SC70 (DCK) example places C3 on V- and C4 on V+ beside the package, the feedback parts next to the inverting input and the output RC (R3, C2) at the output, with ground pour round them.
